title: 1.5 Computing OLS
section: From the SSR curve to the formula
text:
From the SSR curve to the formula
Every choice of slope gives a different SSR; drawn together they form a U-shaped curve. The OLS line sits at the bottom of the curve, where the tangent is flat (derivative = 0).


Figure 1.10. The U-shaped SSR curve


Slope β̂₂  Go to the bottom














Setting the derivative to zero gives two formulas:
\[
\hat\beta_2 = \frac{\sum x_i y_i}{\sum x_i^2}
\qquad\qquad
\hat\beta_1 = \bar Y - \hat\beta_2 \bar X
\]
where \(x_i = X_i - \bar X\) and \(y_i = Y_i - \bar Y\) (deviations from the means).

title: 1.3 Errors, population, and sample
text:
The error term
Each point lies some distance from the line. The regression model writes this distance as the error term, \(u_i\):
\[
Y_i = \underbrace{\beta_1 + \beta_2 X_i}_{\text{value on the line}} + \underbrace{u_i}_{\text{error}}
\]
The error collects every factor other than X that also affects Y, such as household size or habits.


Figure 1.6. Click a point to see its error

text:

The true line applies to the whole population and is unknown. From a sample we can only estimate it. Estimates carry a hat ( ^ ).

title: 1.1 What is regression?
text:
Show print view (PDF)

Preview how the figures look when the page is printed or saved as PDF.
Consider this question: if a household’s income rises, by how much does its consumption rise?
To answer it, we collect data on many households and draw them in a scatter plot. Each point represents one household.
Regression studies how the average value of one variable (Y) changes when another variable (X) changes. The result is summarised by a line.

title: 1.1 What is regression?
text:
Three patterns


Figure 1.2. Positive, negative, and no relationship






PositiveX rises, Y tends to rise






NegativeX rises, Y tends to fall






No relationshipthe line is nearly flat




Examples: income and consumption (positive); price and quantity demanded (negative); shoe size and exam score (no relationship).

title: 1.1 What is regression?
text:
Association is not causation
Ice-cream sales and drowning cases both rise in summer. They are associated, but ice cream does not cause drowning; both are driven by a third factor, hot weather.


Figure 1.3. A hidden third factor


  Hot weather  Ice-cream sales  Drowning cases   affects affects  associated, not causal


Regression shows association. A causal claim needs theory and an appropriate research design.

Regresi mempelajari bagaimana rata-rata Y berubah ketika X berubah.
Garis regresi memiliki intersep (\(\beta_1\)) dan kemiringan (\(\beta_2\)).
Garis regresi melewati rata-rata Y pada setiap X, bukan setiap titik data.

title: 1.4 Gagasan OLS
text:
Mengapa residual dikuadratkan?
Jumlah residual tidak dapat dipakai sebagai ukuran, karena residual positif dan negatif saling meniadakan. Kedua garis berikut sama-sama memiliki jumlah residual nol, padahal Garis B jelas lebih buruk.


Ilustrasi 1.8. Jumlah residual sama-sama nol, kualitas garis berbeda jauh

title: 1.4 Gagasan OLS
text:
Aturan OLS
OLS (Ordinary Least Squares, kuadrat terkecil biasa) memilih garis yang membuat jumlah kuadrat residual (SSR) sekecil mungkin:
\[
\text{SSR} = \sum \hat u_i^2 \;\longrightarrow\; \text{sekecil mungkin}
\]

title: 1.3 Galat, populasi, dan sampel
text:
Galat
Setiap titik memiliki jarak terhadap garis. Model regresi menuliskan jarak ini sebagai galat (error term), \(u_i\):
\[
Y_i = \underbrace{\beta_1 + \beta_2 X_i}_{\text{nilai pada garis}} + \underbrace{u_i}_{\text{galat}}
\]
Galat menampung semua faktor lain di luar X yang ikut memengaruhi Y, misalnya jumlah anggota keluarga atau kebiasaan.


Ilustrasi 1.6. Klik salah satu titik untuk melihat galatnya

title: 1.2 The regression line
text:
A line through the averages
Households with the same income can consume different amounts. The regression line does not pass through every point; it passes through the mean of Y at each value of X, called the conditional mean and written \(E(Y \mid X)\).

title: 1.4 The idea of OLS
text:
Show print view (PDF)

Preview how the figures look when the page is printed or saved as PDF.
A residual is the vertical distance between a data point and the estimated line, \(\hat u_i = Y_i - \hat Y_i\). A good line has small residuals.

title: 1.4 The idea of OLS
text:
Why square the residuals?
The plain sum of residuals is not a useful measure, because positive and negative residuals cancel out. Both lines below have a residual sum of zero, yet Line B is clearly worse.


Figure 1.8. Both residual sums are zero, but the lines differ greatly

title: 1.4 The idea of OLS
text:
The OLS rule
OLS (Ordinary Least Squares) chooses the line that makes the sum of squared residuals (SSR) as small as possible:
\[
\text{SSR} = \sum \hat u_i^2 \;\longrightarrow\; \text{as small as possible}
\]

title: 1.6 Summary and exercise
text:
Regression studies how the mean of Y changes when X changes.
A regression line has an intercept (\(\beta_1\)) and a slope (\(\beta_2\)).
The regression line passes through the mean of Y at each X, not through every data point.
The distance from a point to the line is the error (population) or the residual (sample).
OLS chooses the line with the smallest sum of squared residuals, the bottom of the SSR curve.
Formulas: \(\hat\beta_2 = \sum x_i y_i / \sum x_i^2\) and \(\hat\beta_1 = \bar Y - \hat\beta_2 \bar X\).

title: About this textbook
text:
Using the figures
Each page contains interactive figures in framed boxes: move the sliders, press the buttons, or click points on a chart. The figures work on computers and phones and follow light or dark mode.

title: About this textbook
text:
Print and PDF versions
Every interactive figure has a static counterpart that appears when the page is printed or saved as PDF, with a key message and a link (plus a QR code once the site is published) back to the interactive version. Use the Show print view (PDF) button to preview it, then your browser’s print menu and Save as PDF (preferably in light mode).
